title: Security: Pen Test Results + Patching & SDLC Review - Acme Bank
summary: Redwood and Acme Bank reviewed the recent third-party penetration test findings (redacted); the discussion focused on high/critical findings, proposed mitigations, and alignment on vulnerability management and patch cadence. Acme's team walked through their asset prioritization and asked clarifying questions about Redwood's secure SDLC, dependency scanning, and encryption key handling. Redwood committed to sending a redacted pen test report and a patch cadence template; next steps include a technical deep dive to validate remediation evidence and share SOC 2/ISO artifact mapping for the upcoming audit.
action_items: Maya Patel - send redacted pen test results + executive summary - 2026-03-12
Liam Chen - provide patch cadence template and proposed hardening checklist - 2026-03-13
Rajesh Kumar - provide list of critical assets and SOC contact for remediation evidence - 2026-03-14
next_steps: Send full redacted pen test PDF and summary (Maya) by 2026-03-12
Schedule 60-min technical deep dive to review remediation evidence (week of 2026-03-23) - action: calendar invite from Maya
Share SOC 2/ISO artifact mapping doc and KMS architecture diagram (Liam) by 2026-03-15
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we should be able to keep this to about 45 minutes - 60 max. Maya from Redwood, with Liam our SE.
[00:12] Rajesh Kumar: Yeah thanks Maya. Rajesh here, head of InfoSec at Acme Bank. We circulated the pen test last week - some big stuff in there - wanted to walk through Redwood's plan and how you handle patching/SDLC.
[00:28] Liam Chen: Great, thanks Rajesh. Quick call agenda: we'll do a high-level overview of the findings you flagged, talk cadence for vuln mgmt, then cover SDLC/dependency scanning and KMS/encryption + RBAC.
[00:40] Emily Chu: Hi, Emily - infra lead. We also want to confirm audit log retention and SSO requirements.
[00:46] Sofia Martinez: Sofia from compliance - focusing on SOC 2 evidence and timelines.
[00:51] Maya Patel: Perfect. Rajesh do you want to kick off with the highest severity items you want to prioritize?
[00:56] Rajesh Kumar: Sure. So the pen test called out three critical - two RCE-like chaining things in the model-serving path, and one misconfigured S3 bucket that contained staging assets. Also some dependency vulnerabilities flagged in an older library used by the agent controller.
[01:14] Liam Chen: Okay, thanks. Couple of clarifications: the model-serving RCE pathways - are those across the hosted API or a dedicated deployment?
[01:23] Rajesh Kumar: This was tested against a Dedicated environment we spun up in the pen test harness; that said the vuln looked like it stemmed from how the KV cache handles untrusted input and a deserialization edge case.
[01:36] Liam Chen: Understood. In Redwood's runtime we have defenses - input sanitization at the request layer, runtime sandboxing in the worker image, and we recently rolled out an extra deserialization check in the last patch. I'll put the patch version in the notes.
[01:48] Maya Patel: We also have a mitigations timeline we can share. The red team report included exploitation PoCs, so we'll redact that for you but send the sanitized findings.
[01:56] Rajesh Kumar: That would help - we need to show remediation paths to our board and our auditors.
[02:02] Sofia Martinez: For SOC 2 we need evidence of remediation timeliness and patch cadences, also RBAC enforcement logs.
[02:09] Emily Chu: On the S3, we took a look and that one was a staging bucket created during internal testing; it should have been blocked by the infra provisioning scripts. We'll include the IaC commit and remediation PR id.
[02:21] Liam Chen: Good, that's helpful. On the dependency vulnerabilities, are these transitive libs - like older protobuf or a JS package - or something in the C++ runtime?
[02:32] Rajesh Kumar: Looks like a transitive NPM vuln flagged by Snyk for the admin UI.
[02:37] Maya Patel: For the admin UI we recommend isolating it behind customer-managed VPC and add WAF rules; we can share our secure SDLC checklist that mandates dependency scanning in CI and blocking PRs for critical CVEs.
[02:50] Rajesh Kumar: Can you walk through your secure SDLC - specifically SCA tooling, cadence of scans, and how you enforce fixes?
[02:58] Liam Chen: Sure. We run dependency scanning on every PR with Snyk and GitHub Actions; critical CVEs block the merge unless there's a compensating control. We track tickets in our backlog system and have a weekly triage for vuln severity. For customer-facing infra we keep a 30-day SLA for critical fixes, 90 days for high.
[03:17] Sofia Martinez: Do you have a formal change advisory/patch calendar we can map to our GRC controls?
[03:23] Maya Patel: Yes - we'll share a patch cadence template - typical cadence is monthly security patches for non-critical and immediate hotfix for critical. For Dedicated customers we offer a configurable patch window to avoid impacting SLAs; we can do maintenance windows that align with Acme's nominated blackout windows.
[03:38] Emily Chu: Important for us: rollback process and canary deploys. If a patch breaks model latency we need an automated rollback.
[03:45] Liam Chen: We do canaries by default for runtime patches; if the canary fails we automatically roll back to the previous image and surface metrics. We'll include our runbook excerpts.
[03:55] Rajesh Kumar: Audit logs - we need 12 months retention for access logs and SSO events, and proof that KMS keys are customer-scoped for private deployments.
[04:05] Maya Patel: For Private/VPC we support customer-managed KMS; keys are in your KMS and we don't store plaintext. Audit logs can be exported to your logging stack (we support S3/GCS and SIEM integrations). Retention is configurable and we can push exported logs to your storage with 12+ months retention.
[04:22] Sofia Martinez: How about encryption at rest for embeddings and KV cache? Are they encrypted with customer keys?
[04:29] Liam Chen: Embeddings and KV cache are encrypted at rest. For Private we can use your KMS; for hosted we use our managed KMS but offer customer-managed keys for enterprise. We will detail the crypto algorithms and key rotation policy in the artifact we send.
[04:44] Rajesh Kumar: Do you provide audit-ready artifacts for SOC 2 - e.g., change logs, code review evidence, pen test summaries?
[04:52] Maya Patel: Yes - we have an SOC 2 artifact bundle we share under NDA. It includes change logs, PR review stats, dependency scanning reports, and pen test exec summaries. We'll attach an artifact mapping doc to the next email.
[05:03] Emily Chu: On RBAC and SSO - we need SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning, and role granularity so op teams can't export logs outside the bank's logging accounts.
[05:14] Liam Chen: We support SAML + SCIM and fine-grained RBAC; roles can be scoped per-tenant and per-resource. Exports require explicit permission; we can also require MFA for export workflows.
[05:25] Rajesh Kumar: One ask: we want continuous vuln scanning on the runtime image - do you run image scanning?
[05:31] Liam Chen: Yes, we run container image scanning on build and on base-image updates, and we have a weekly cascade job that rescans images when new CVEs are published. Critical CVEs trigger immediate rebuilds.
[05:43] Maya Patel: To be explicit about timelines: critical findings - 24 to 72 hours triage and mitigation plan; critical fixes pushed within 30 days unless a hotfix is required sooner. High severity - 90 day remediation target. We'll include our SLA language.
[05:58] Sofia Martinez: For the pen test items we need evidence that fixes are applied - PRs, CVE tracker updates, and re-test notes.
[06:04] Liam Chen: Agreed - we'll provide links to PRs and ticket numbers once redaction is complete. For any items requiring code changes we'll share branch names and short diffs.
[06:14] Rajesh Kumar: Can you also outline how you manage third-party dependencies for model weights and any external repos? We need to know provenance and scanning.
[06:24] Liam Chen: Model weights are validated with checksums and stored in immutable object storage; any third-party weights are tagged and we run periodic integrity checks. Dependencies used during model compilation are part of our SBOM and we can provide per-release SBOMs.
[06:38] Emily Chu: Perfect. A question on vulnerability disclosure - if we find an issue, what's the reporting channel and SLA?
[06:44] Maya Patel: We have a dedicated security intake email and a ticketing pipeline; for customers we offer a priority channel and weekly updates until closure. SLA for initial response is 24 hours.
[06:54] Rajesh Kumar: Good. Last area: rollback evidence and canary metrics - we need to see latency/throughput graphs during deploys.
[07:02] Liam Chen: We can provide short-term dashboards for the canary period and stored traces for 30 days; summary metrics can be included in the evidence bundle.
[07:11] Sofia Martinez: Timeline recap?
[07:13] Maya Patel: Action items: we'll send a redacted pen test summary and the SOC artifact mapping by Friday 2026-03-12; Liam will send the patch cadence template and secure SDLC checklist by 2026-03-13; then we'll schedule the technical remediation deep dive for week of 2026-03-23.
[07:30] Rajesh Kumar: That works. Appreciate the partnership.
[07:33] Emily Chu: Thanks everyone.
[07:35] Maya Patel: Thanks all - we'll follow up in email with the links. Linking the pen test: [drive]/acme/pen-test-2026-redacted.pdf (private link).
[07:44] Sofia Martinez: And please include the SOC 2 mapping.
[07:46] Maya Patel: Will do.
[07:48] [call ends]
